mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% for two consecutive months signals the Fed is likely to pause or reverse rate hikes, lowering discount rates and boosting equity valuations, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% and remains above for ≥2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day pre-inflation spike average (t-test p > 0.05) during the inflation breakout period.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% in a single month, the expected discount rate on future cash flows increases, reducing the present value of equities and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for 60-day horizon remains above 0.05 over a 12-month window of such FEDFUNDS moves.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in PAYEMS (labor market additions) of at least 50,000 jobs over three months indicates labor market resilience, which supports corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly average ≥ +50,000 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during the window are not statistically outperforming the prior 5-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO falls by more than 2% in a month, it signals supply-side weakness, raising uncertainty and compressing equity valuations, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: During such INDPRO declines, 20-day forward returns do not fall below the 2-week rolling average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly increase in HOUST (household spending) of at least 2% suggests resilient consumer demand, which elevates earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly average ≥ +2% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Stable or improving consumer demand cycle
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns during the window are not significantly higher than the prior 30-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous monthly increases in both GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) above their 12-month moving averages by at least 1% each indicate robust demand across sectors, which tends to produce positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > GDPC1_12m_avg and RSAFS > RSAFS_12m_avg, both by ≥ +1%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive relative to the 12-month pre-signal average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (as signaled by a 4-month declining trend in FEDFUNDS), the S&P 500 exhibits a positive 60-day forward return due to lower financing costs and improved risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS 4-month simple moving average is declining
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns during easing periods are not significantly higher than during neutral FEDFUNDS trends (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in UNRATE (unemployment rate) above 4% for two consecutive months is interpreted as a labor market cooling, which typically precedes a pullback in equities and predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE monthly average > +4% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during the over-heating episode are not statistically lower than during normal unemployment regimes (t-test p > 0.05).
